subject.title: Exec provider: 1Password op CLI spawns daemon processes, hangs on macOS Tahoe (needs --cache=false)

question: Should the 1Password cache-daemon workaround be handled as docs/config guidance using existing exec provider fields, or should OpenClaw add runtime behavior for this provider?
rationale: The docs-only path is narrow and already supported, while automatic `op` detection or env injection changes credential command policy in core.

options.title: Document existing workaround
options.body: Update the 1Password exec-provider docs to show `--cache=false` before `read` or `OP_CACHE=false` in provider `env`, with LaunchAgent/TCC context.

options.title: Design a generic exec-provider guard
options.body: Keep this open for a broader policy that applies to side-effecting credential CLIs without hardcoding 1Password.

options.title: Add provider-specific runtime injection
options.body: Teach core to recognize the 1Password CLI and disable its cache automatically, accepting a provider-specific credential policy in core.

recommendation.title: Document existing workaround
recommendation.body: Update the 1Password exec-provider docs to show `--cache=false` before `read` or `OP_CACHE=false` in provider `env`, with LaunchAgent/TCC context.

likelyOwner.reason: Most directly tied to the current 1Password SecretRef docs and generic exec-provider implementation history.
